Read https://openrouter.ai/docs/features/prompt-caching (and if it links to it, https://openrouter.ai/docs/use-cases/usage-accounting) and answer concisely, quoting the docs where possible:
1. Which providers cache prompts AUTOMATICALLY (no request changes) — especially OpenAI models, Google Gemini models, DeepSeek, xAI — and their minimum prompt size / how long cached entries live.
2. Which need explicit `cache_control` breakpoints (Anthropic, others?) and how they are placed (system message / content parts, max number of breakpoints, TTL options).
3. What matters for cache hits: the prompt PREFIX must be identical? Are tool definitions part of the cached prefix? Any note about provider routing/sticky routing affecting cache hits.
4. How cached tokens show up in the response usage (field names like prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens, cache_write_tokens), and how the discount is reported (cache_discount / cost).
5. In usage accounting: what `usage: { include: true }` returns (cost field name, units = USD credits?), and whether it is still needed or now always returned.
Give the answer as a short structured list.

input.message:
Sources read: https://openrouter.ai/docs/features/prompt-caching (full page, no truncation). It links to the usage accounting page at https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/administration/usage-accounting.md (the caller's suggested /docs/use-cases/usage-accounting path was not fetched; the page links to the cookbook path instead). Both pages were fetched from a non-preapproved source, so quotes are kept short.

1. AUTOMATIC caching (no request changes)
- General: "Most providers automatically enable prompt caching, but note that some (see Alibaba and Anthropic below) require you to enable it on a per-message basis."
- OpenAI: automatic, "does not require any additional configuration. There is a minimum prompt size of 1024 tokens." Cache lifetime is not stated in the caching page for automatic caching. Explicit-mode TTL is 30m default or 12h.
- Google Gemini 2.5+ (implicit): no cache_control needed. "Note that the TTL is on average 3-5 minutes, but will vary." Minimum: 1024 tokens for Gemini 2.5 Flash, 4096 for Gemini 2.5 Pro. (A later Gemini section says cache writes use a "5 minute TTL that does not update.")
- DeepSeek: "automated and does not require any additional configuration." No minimum or TTL stated.
- xAI/Grok: "automated and does not require any additional configuration." No minimum or TTL stated. (The page uses the heading "Grok".)
- Also automatic: Moonshot AI, Groq (Kimi K2 only), Z.AI (no minimum or TTL stated).

2. EXPLICIT cache_control (or equivalent) needed
- Anthropic Claude: "Place cache_control directly on individual content blocks" (explicit). Max "a limit of four explicit breakpoints." Top-level automatic caching is also available: a single top-level "cache_control": {"type":"ephemeral"} that places the breakpoint on the last cacheable block. TTL: default 5 minutes (`{"type":"ephemeral"}`) or 1 hour (`"ttl": "1h"`). Minimum cacheable length varies by model: 512 (e.g., Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5), 1,024, 2,048, or 4,096 tokens depending on the model.
- Alibaba Qwen: explicit cache_control on content blocks, 5-minute TTL only. Limited to listed models.
- Google Gemini: explicit cache_control breakpoints are also required for caching on OpenRouter, even though implicit caching exists. "There is not a limit on the number of cache_control breakpoints... OpenRouter will use only the last breakpoint for Gemini caching." Gemini has a 5-minute TTL that does not update.
- OpenAI GPT-5.6+ explicit mode (optional): `prompt_cache_breakpoint` on text blocks plus request-level `prompt_cache_options` {"mode":"explicit","ttl":"30m"|"12h"}. Only supported on GPT-5.6 and newer.
- Placement: system or user message content parts (text blocks). The Gemini note says cache_control inside the first system message caches the system instruction, and a dynamic tail should go in a later user message.

3. Cache-hit requirements
- Prefix rule: the page says "keep the initial portion of your message arrays consistent between requests. Push variations ... toward the end." It does not use the phrase "identical prefix" explicitly, but that is the implication.
- Tool definitions: the caching page does not say whether tools are part of the cached prefix. Not stated.
- Sticky routing: OpenRouter routes follow-up requests to the same provider endpoint after a cached request. "Sticky sessions expire after 60 minutes of inactivity." It only activates when "the provider's cache read pricing is cheaper than regular prompt pricing." It is disabled if you set `provider.order`. Default conversation key: a hash of the first system/developer message and the first non-system message. Passing `session_id` (body or `x-session-id` header, max 256 chars) sets the key explicitly, and sticky routing then starts on any successful request. Fallback key: `prompt_cache_key`. Auto/Pareto routers may also reuse the resolved model.

4. Usage fields and discount
- Chat Completions: `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` (read) and `usage.prompt_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens` (written).
- Responses API: `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens`.
- Discount: "The `cache_discount` field in the response body will tell you how much the response saved on cache usage." Note: the usage-accounting page's examples do not show a `cache_discount` field, only `cost` and `cost_details`. Treat `cache_discount` as the caching page's claim, unverified against the examples.
- Cost breakdown: `cost` is the total charged. `cost_details.upstream_inference_cost` is the upstream provider cost; it splits into `upstream_inference_input_cost` and `upstream_inference_output_cost` (Responses), or `upstream_inference_prompt_cost` and `upstream_inference_completions_cost` (Chat Completions).
- Cancelled streams usually get no cache discount.

5. Usage accounting (`usage: { include: true }`)
- It is NOT needed anymore. The page says: "On Chat Completions, the `usage: { include: true }` and `stream_options: { include_usage: true }` parameters are deprecated and have no effect... Full usage details are always included automatically in every response on both APIs."
- Cost field: `cost` at the usage level. Units: the docs say "Cost in credits". Their stream example prints "Cost: 0.005616 credits". They do not explicitly say USD, so that is not confirmed from these pages.
- Also returned: `is_byok`, `cost_details`, and `deferred_tools_details` (for universal-profile tool loops).
- Generation endpoint: the `/api/v1/generation` endpoint can also return usage by generation id. `upstream_inference_cost` there is only populated for BYOK requests.

Final URLs read:
- https://openrouter.ai/docs/features/prompt-caching
- https://openrouter.ai/docs/cookbook/administration/usage-accounting.md
